question: Can raw 000 or 111 write a retained signal in one of the original six distinctions without a write command, and can a separate knot respond to that signal after the same later input?

public_inputs.original: Order abcxyz, hard NAE on abc, ayz, xbz, xyc. The original xyz never equals 000 or 111. Supply independent raw observations u,v,w, atomically as a whole word. They may be generated by the predecessor's relaxed source. They are not assignments to the original xyz.
public_inputs.coupling: Three permanently present NAE rules (u,a,x), (v,a,x), (w,a,x). The externally supplied items are the wiring, a prepared clear start, the law for changing a bit and the downstream wiring. No storage beyond the six original values. Start with a!=x,y=0 in a hard-legal core; use both such starts. Check the two y=1 rest states as loaded controls.
public_inputs.update: Each independent attempt chooses one of the six core distinctions uniformly. Accept the flip iff the four hard rules allow it and it introduces no newly violated input coupling compared to the current state under the same raw word. Previously violated couplings may be repaired; changing raw word does not itself flip or overwrite the core. Self-loops include rejected proposals. At constant input starting in a compatible state this is exactly the legal flip rule. Kernel is calculated from local NAE values; equality of the three inputs is never tested in the update.
public_inputs.retention: Baseline permits either flip direction. Separately test a constant one-way response of the original read distinction y (block 1-to-0 permanently); no further history variable. This preference is active under every input and in the absence of an event. The other five distinctions are reversible. No phase in either dynamics.
public_inputs.reading: Use a fresh NAE(y,p,q) with initially mixed pq=01, all inputs common after exposure. Trying q=0 at p=0 succeeds if the stored y permits it. Evaluate every upper word; if y is replaced by an independent bit the probe has no access to the record.

forbidden_inputs: No externally computed event flag, per-word write instruction, acknowledgment, feedback about hidden values, wait-until-captured stopping rule or target-dependent clock.
No unconstrained jump in the six-bit state when an input changes, training labels, or externally set memory after initialization.
No raw input or incident-gate state given to the upper probe. The scorer alone classifies events to measure performance.
primary_observable: For both clear starts and both polarities, compute the exact probability of capture versus residence time under the same proposal rule for all words and a common mixed background. Require zero false writes on every mixed-only sequence, test retention and later differential allowed response. For sustained exposure use terminal classes to decide probability-one capture; for finite pulses disclose all miss probabilities. Identify whether one flag can report the event polarity.
cheapest_meaningful_control: Compare reversible core to the constant one-way preference. Remove a raw coupling or reverse one raw sign, hold a mixed background through the identical schedule, and disconnect the downstream knot. Test the historical bare model where the external word has no coupling.
decision_or_followup_rule: A pulse-triggered record requires a positive chance of retained and usable capture for both 000 and 111, zero false positives starting clear under all mixed-only arrival orders, and a matched later query that distinguishes written from clear. Report finite-latency and sustained/repeated-event guarantees only where verified. A positive with the one-way preference is conditional on this supplied law.
resource_budget: Exact finite analysis of 18 six-bit core states by eight raw words. Check finite pulses at 0,1,2,4,8,16,32,64 and 128 proposals with integer counts or rational arithmetic, and absorption by finite-state reachability/rational equations. Standard-library CPU. No sampled learn/test split or fitted weights.
first_executable_signal: Mixed inputs should freeze the initially opposite pair, and an equal word should enable at least one hard-legal change. Verify whether y ever changes and whether a mixed reset can accept the post-event state without externally forcing the core.
stop_rule: Run the finite exposure/readout, mixture and control cases, preserve failures, check by a separate implementation, and close the bounded ticket.
nonclaims: The raw word is external and simultaneous. The static four-knot relation supplies no law of time or sensor attachment.

The optional one-way preference and chosen permanent geometry are supplied. A remembered counterexample is not a general algorithm for discovering the hidden rule, and absence of a capture is not proof of absence of events.
A next-level allowed relation is a finite transfer test, not an unbounded hierarchy.
feasibility_disclosure: The predecessor's 18 states, its two held memory states and its complete indistinguishable histories were already known. Feasibility enumeration of this symmetric attachment found four compatible isolated core states at mixed inputs and one connected set of eleven compatible states at either equal input. One-way capture, finite pulse probabilities, reopening under new words, and downstream controls have not been measured in this identity.
